title: Report a failure together with its suppressed close failures

blocks.text: When the body of a try-with-resources throws and closing the resource throws too, the body's exception is the one thrown; the close exception is added to it as *suppressed*, and `getSuppressed()` returns it. Overlooking suppressed exceptions is one of the page's pitfalls.
Write `LogWriter.write(Opener opener, String text)`. It opens the channel named `"log"`, writes `text` to it, and closes it. It returns:

items: otherwise `"failed: " + message` of the `IOException` that was thrown, followed by `"; suppressed: " + message` for each exception in its `getSuppressed()`, in that array's order.

blocks.text: Anything other than an `IOException` is not reported: it reaches the caller.
A failure while closing counts as a failure too.

cases.says: A write that succeeds reports ok, and the channel is closed.
A write failure is reported with its message.
When closing also fails, try-with-resources suppresses that failure into the write's, and the report lists it.
A close failure after a good write is the failure itself, and it is reported, not swallowed.
Only an IOException is reported; an unchecked failure reaches the caller, after the channel is closed.

concepts: When the body and a close both throw, the body's exception is thrown and the close exception is attached to it as suppressed.
